html:
Swayambhunath is a Buddhist stupa on a hill west of Kathmandu in Nepal, dating back at least to the 5th century, in the time of the Licchavi kings.

Legend says the valley was once a lake, and a lotus that grew from it gave off a light that became the "self-arisen" Swayambhu. Its white dome is crowned by a gilded tower painted with the eyes of the Buddha, an image now used across Nepal. Visitors call it the Monkey Temple for the monkeys that live there.

Newar Buddhists of the valley and Tibetan pilgrims both worship there, showing how Buddhism lived on in Nepal long after it faded in India. It is part of the Kathmandu Valley World Heritage Site and was damaged in the earthquake of 2015.
sum: Swayambhunath is a Buddhist stupa on a hill west of Kathmandu in Nepal, dating back at least to the 5th century, in the time of the Licchavi kings.
